alternativeExplanations: The addendum attributes the announced CAD 53.6 million increase to restored support for disability, senior and education programs (printed page 1).
A budget addendum is a documented revision, not by itself an unexplained overrun.
confirmedFacts: Both inputs are estimates for fiscal 2026–27 in the same budget presentation.
The reported plan changed; this does not establish actual expenditure.
limitations: Not the latest forecast.
Original budget URL has an unresolved access hold; values were independently checked before that hold.
Source text was reviewed, but raw document binaries were not retained.
missingEvidence: No linked appropriation or legislative-vote record has been validated in this workflow.
No contract, invoice, cash payment or delivered outcome is joined to this change.
The later September forecast tables are not integrated.
nextSteps: Reconcile addendum program detail to the precise summary difference.
Link the exact approval record and subsequent actuals using compatible accounting definitions.
investigations.question: How did the reported spending plan change, and can those plans be followed through to payments and delivery?

responses.summary: The government describes reinstated and re-established support for disability, senior and education programs; the introduction rounds the change to CAD 53.6 million.

investigations.summary: The 2026–27 addendum increased planned departmental expenses by CAD 53.592 million. This is a change to estimates, not evidence of money paid, waste or wrongdoing.
investigations.title: What changed between the original budget and its addendum?
investigations.whyFlagged: An explicit comparison of the same fiscal-year departmental-expense row in two separately identified budget versions.
